findings.reason: the node as written sends the repair at six modules while its gate requires touching twenty, and the one derived-edge reader needs a replacement mechanism the plan does not state, so the section would fail its own done-when or destroy successor resolution.
findings.text: §16 scopes the removal to "the modules the successor-derivation record names" (the census, `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/row-census.html:70`, states this as "six modules"), but its own done-when asserts "`superseded_by` has no reader in the tree", which the cited record contradicts: that record enumerates 42 reader lines across 20 files and names surfaces outside the six production modules — the LinkML declaration at `schemas/standard_name.yaml:925`, its three generated artefacts, a documentation row and nine test files — and reports that `graph_ops.py:3193` derives the `HAS_SUCCESSOR` edges *from* the scalar, so removing that read removes the very edge §16 relies on to resolve successors; a worker following the six-module scope cannot close the "no reader" gate, and a worker that instead strips every occurrence risks the edge derivation.

findings.reason: §6's census exists to replace recorded figures with live ones, and a repair or scoping decision resting on 334 would understate the population by 78 names.
findings.text: §2 states "334 live names are labelled scaffolding while carrying reviewed documentation", and §1's lead paragraph repeats "334 live names", but the census §6 cites gives `Recorded: … 334 … Live: {"docs_acc_nonempty": 412} … the misleading derived-while-documented population is now 412` (`docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/row-census.html:136-137`); 334 is the recorded figure and §17 uses the correct live figure, 412, for the same population, so the plan carries two different "live" counts for one defect.

findings.reason: the node cannot be closed on one verdict, since either guard can land and pass while the other is absent or still-unfixed, and its single gate proves neither fix.
findings.text: §14 is one node carrying two independent release-path fixes with two independent guards: an edits-scoped `sn run` honouring `--skip-global-maintenance` in `imas_codex/cli/sn.py`, and an export that filters every candidate refusing instead of exiting 0, whose done-when itself separates into "one test … and one shows …".

findings.reason: one verdict cannot close a node whose two results point at different follow-on repairs, and a partial result is unclassifiable.
findings.text: §15 is headed "Two measurements before repair" and carries (a) a reproduction of the compose-supersede failure over a dual-bound source and (b) a re-derivation of the unsourced-ancestry census, two unrelated measurements whose results each "decide whether a repair section follows".

findings.reason: §6 establishes the fragment directory convention, so the worker has a durable home and the omission is a naming tightening rather than a redirect.
findings.text: §15's done-when requires that "an evidence fragment records both" measurements but names no path for it, unlike §6 which names `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/row-census.html`.
